page: Microsoft Azure F4-2amds_v7 is a constrained-vCPU instance within the compute-focused Famdsv7 family, tailored for deployments requiring substantial per-core memory and fast clock speeds. The virtual machine runs under Microsoft Hyper-V and is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs operating at frequencies up to 4.5 GHz, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. The processor incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. System memory totals 32.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local temporary storage is bundled as a 472 GB NVMe solid-state drive, while no dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs are included.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier single-threaded compute efficiency. In Geekbench single-core testing, the instance achieved a score of 2819.0, accompanied by a top-tier stress-ng single-core score of 3779.98. Single-threaded data handling benchmarks also reflect this strength, with gzip throughput reaching 40.7 GB/s and bzip3 decompression achieving 18.14 GB/s. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics scale within the boundaries of its 2-core configuration, showing average stress-ng multi-core (7529.66) and Geekbench multi-core (5085.0) outcomes. Clang compilation and multi-threaded decompression fall into lower percentiles due to limited parallel thread count. Memory throughput registers 430.09 GB/s in cached reads and 53.06 GB/s across large-block uncached reads, supporting 7.35 million Redis SET operations per second.

The hardware configuration trades broad multi-threaded scaling for high memory allocation per core and single-core execution speed. This balance provides qualitative cost efficiency for software stacks licensed per CPU core that require significant memory footprints and high frequency execution. The integrated 472 GB NVMe drive offers high-speed scratch space to eliminate network storage latency for temporary files. Primary tradeoffs involve restricted multi-core parallel capacity and modest static web serving throughput. Appropriate workloads include per-core licensed relational databases, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, memory-intensive ETL pipelines, and lightweight model inference.
description: Microsoft Azure F4-2amds_v7 is a compute-oriented virtual machine configured with constrained vCPU capacity to optimize memory allocation per core. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor built on x86_64 architecture, it delivers 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs clocked at 4.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high density of 16.0 GB per vCPU, alongside a 472 GB local NVMe SSD. No GPUs are attached. Benchmark measurements show top-tier single-core performance across Geekbench and stress-ng, accompanied by strong single-threaded data compression and solid memory bandwidth. Multi-core throughput is constrained by the two-core allocation. By pairing high clock speeds with substantial RAM and fast NVMe storage, this instance is suitable for per-core licensed databases, in-memory caching systems, data processing pipelines, and memory-intensive single-threaded workloads.
